Summary: This specification enables content creators to cryptographically bind their verified identity to C2PA-signed digital assets. It supports multiple identity binding methods including X.509 certificates and Identity Claim Aggregators (ICA). Ratified by the Decentralized Identity Foundation (DIF) on December 15, 2025, after CAWG formally became a DIF working group in March 2025. Directly extends and complements the C2PA Specification and CAWG Metadata specification.

This specification provides normative UX guidance for how applications should display Content Credentials to end users. It defines presentation rules for provenance indicators, trust signals, and identity claims in user interfaces, ensuring consistent and trustworthy communication of C2PA content credentials across products and platforms. Ratified by DIF on February 5, 2026.

Summary: This W3C Recommendation (published May 15, 2025) provides a standard data model for cryptographically secure, privacy-respecting, machine-verifiable credentials. It is directly applicable to content authenticity workflows — notably as the foundation for identity binding in CAWG Identity Assertions. The v2.0 family comprises seven interlocking specifications covering the data model, JSON-LD contexts, and securing mechanisms (ECDSA and BBS). Supersedes v1.1.

Summary: This NIST technical report provides authoritative US government guidance on detecting, authenticating, and labeling AI-generated and synthetic content. It covers digital watermarking, metadata-based provenance, and content labeling approaches, with explicit interoperability references to C2PA and W3C PROV as recommended standards. Although a technical report rather than a normative standard, it carries significant influence on US policy and industry practice for AI content authenticity.

Summary: Published at the AI for Good Global Summit on July 11, 2025 by the ISO/IEC/ITU AI and Multimedia Authenticity Standards (AMAS) collaboration. Provides the authoritative international landscape map of all standards relevant to AI-generated content authenticity, covering content provenance, watermarking, detection, and rights declarations. An accompanying Policy Paper addresses regulatory guidance. Essential reference document for understanding the global standards ecosystem in this domain.

Name of Standard/Specification: ISO/IEC 21000-3:2025 — MPEG-21 Part 3: Digital Item Identification
Summary: This 2025 edition of MPEG-21 Part 3 replaces the original 2003 version and defines a framework for the unique identification of digital items and their components. It provides persistent, globally unique identifiers for digital content objects and is applicable across audio, video, images, and documents. Relevant to asset identifier workflows and interoperable with C2PA, ISCC, and GMI (IWA 44) identification schemes.

Name of Standard/Specification: EU AI Act Article 50 — AI-Generated Content Disclosure Requirements
Summary: Article 50 of the EU Artificial Intelligence Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, entered into force August 1, 2024) mandates disclosure and machine-readable labeling for AI-generated synthetic content, including deepfakes. Providers of general-purpose AI systems must ensure outputs are marked in a machine-readable format detectable as artificially generated. Harmonized technical standards for compliance (via CEN-CENELEC JTC21) are being fast-tracked for publication by Q4 2026. Though regulatory rather than a technical standard, this is the primary legal driver for AI content authenticity requirements in Europe.

The C2PA Conformance Program, officially launched June 4, 2025, provides a live, publicly accessible Trust List of certified signers and a Conforming Products List of validated implementations of the C2PA Specification. It establishes the governance and verification infrastructure necessary for relying parties to validate C2PA manifests in production environments. An essential operational complement to the C2PA Specification itself.
